title: A Small Client
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Yokomizo) omitted by convention, same as ep011. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges between the entities involved. The old cases/ep354-355_a_small_client.json file had the correct culprit (Bessho Toshiko / old id s2) and its two clues were both directionally correct (mole-location mismatch, video started early) -- no reversed clue found here, unlike some other rebuilds. What it missed: (1) the entire client subplot -- Kinukawa Kazuki, the 6-year-old actor who hired the agency, was omitted as a node entirely even though he drives part one and the case's emotional resolution; (2) the B-plot twist that Saegusa Tomoko (old file's s3, listed only as a bare suspect) is actually Kazuki's real biological mother, who wrote him the genuine 'Atsuko'-signed postcards and deliberately acted cold so he wouldn't recognize her -- this is a distinct, deliberate reveal in the finale, not just unresolved suspicion; (3) Izumiya, the tabloid chief editor Kamoshita phoned ~10 minutes before the murder, whose testimony supplies the timeline and the blackmail context; (4) the second weapon -- Kamoshita was struck unconscious with a shower nozzle (luminol-positive) before being strangled with videotape stretched into a cord, not strangled outright; (5) that Bessho's extortion of Kazuki's production company (20 million yen, posing as his mother 'Atsuko') was itself a con -- she isn't his mother and admits the murderer's father story was a lie too, which is the actual motive engine (Kamoshita threatened to blackmail her for life over the hoax). Person name spelling follows the on-screen character cards (Saegusa Tomoko, Bessho Toshiko, Kusano Mitsu) rather than the old file's 'Tomoka Saegusa' ordering. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The crime-scene photo shows a red mark on the culprit's left chest, but Kusano's real mole is on her right chest, Bessho's is on her cheek, and Saegusa's is on the back of her neck -- none match, so the mark can't be an actual mole.

Kamoshita's rented cassette runs only 93 minutes against its 94-minute box label and starts straight at the opening title, missing the logos and prologue a fresh store copy of the same film has -- the missing minute of tape became the murder weapon.

Every postcard uses only the top-left quarter of the same four-part scenic postcard set sold at this inn, never the other three sections or any other sight -- deliberate concealment of the sender's workplace, pointing to an inn insider.

Kazuki recalls hearing a knife chopping rhythmically while gazing at his mother's mole -- if she'd been holding him face-to-face her hands couldn't have been cooking, so he must have been carried on her back and glimpsed the mole on her neck, not her chest.
